short: Swedish Field Marshal and artillery innovator who led the army to its greatest late-war victories despite crippling gout.
full:
Lennart Torstensson (1603–1651) revolutionized seventeenth-century warfare through his innovative use of highly mobile field artillery. Having served as Gustavus Adolphus's artillery commander at Breitenfeld and Alte Veste, he spent a year in Imperial captivity which ruined his health. He succeeded Banér as commander of the Swedish army in Germany in 1641.

Despite suffering from such severe gout that he often commanded from a litter, Torstensson's campaigns were defined by lightning-fast marches and aggressive maneuvers. He annihilated Imperial armies at the Second Battle of Breitenfeld in 1642 and at Jankau in 1645, bringing Swedish forces to the very gates of Vienna. He was forced to resign his command in 1646 due to his failing health.
